observations: Photo 0: Front view of a black Dell monitor on a wooden stool. The screen is off. The Dell logo is visible at the bottom center of the bezel. A watermark 'NEWARK TECHNOLOGY' is overlaid.
Photo 1: Rear view of the same monitor. The Dell logo is embossed on the back panel. The stand is attached. A white iMac is visible in the background.

Photo 2: Slightly angled front view of the monitor, showing the screen and bezel. The Dell logo is visible at the bottom. A black rectangular object (possibly a remote or power adapter) rests on the stool in front of the monitor.
All photos show the monitor in a dimly lit indoor environment with visible clutter in the background.

claims.evidence: Dell brand visible on bezel (photo 0) and back (photo 1). The size is not directly readable, but the physical proportions and bezel thickness are consistent with a 17-inch monitor. The seller's claim is plausible and not contradicted by the photos.

risks.risk: Monitor does not power on or has dead pixels/defects on screen
risks.proof: A video clip showing the monitor powered on, displaying a test pattern or image, with no visible dead pixels, flickering, or color distortion.
Photo showing all included accessories, including power cable, VGA/HDMI cable, and any other connectors.

risks.risk: Physical damage not visible in photos (e.g., cracks, deep scratches, or bent stand)
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the screen surface, bezel edges, and stand from multiple angles.
risks.if_unproven: priced as having hidden physical damage

proof_requests: Video clip of the monitor powered on and displaying an image.
Photo of all included cables and accessories.
Close-up photos of the screen and stand for damage inspection.
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a Dell monitor, and the seller's claim is supported. However, critical functional and condition risks (working state, accessories, physical damage) cannot be verified from the current photos. Without proof of functionality and completeness, the item cannot be priced accurately and must be assessed as potentially non-working or incomplete.
